instantiated_cells.justification: Section 101.99 makes violations of §101.71(A)-(C) and §101.77 misdemeanors of the fourth degree, and knowingly filing a false statement under §101.71(D) a misdemeanor of the first degree; §101.72(G) also imposes late filing fees of $12.50/day up to $100, establishing that penalties are provided for by law.

The statute requires only that the executive director "review" each registration statement for completeness (§101.72(G), §121.62(G)) and permits the Attorney General to "investigate compliance" upon apparent violations (§101.79, §121.69), but nowhere mandates a systematic audit of lobbying disclosure filings.

content.text:
I'll analyze the statute text for the two enforcement-related cells.

**Cell 1: lobbying_violation_penalties_imposed_in_practice (legal)** — This asks de jure whether the statute provides for penalties for lobbying violations. Section 101.99 establishes misdemeanor penalties (4th degree for most violations, 1st degree for filing false statements), and §101.71, §101.91, §101.77, §101.97 define the violations. There are also late filing fees in §101.72(G). Penalties clearly exist in law.

**Cell 2: lobbying_disclosure_audit_required_in_law (legal)** — Looking for any requirement for audits of lobbying disclosures. The statute provides for review of registration statements by the executive director (§101.72(G), §101.92(G), §121.62(G)) and investigation of violations by the Attorney General (§101.79, §121.69), but no mandatory audit of disclosure filings is established.
